hero.label: Developer guide
hero.title: Seedance 2.5 API: access, pricing and code examples
hero.description: You can call Seedance 2.5 today through third-party API providers such as Kie and fal. On October 3, 2026, Kie listed $0.14 per second at 480p and $0.315 at 720p, and fal listed about $0.22 and $0.47. A request is one asynchronous job: create a task, then poll or receive a callback.
hero.verdict: Kie is the cheaper of the two routes we reviewed and uses one request shape for text, image and reference inputs. fal splits those into three endpoints and ships a queue SDK. Keep either one behind your own server-side adapter.
hero.last_reviewed: Schema reviewed October 12, 2026 · prices dated October 3
hero.source_note: API schemas rechecked October 12, 2026; price examples retain their October 3 snapshot date. Account pricing can change. This site provides a browser workspace and does not offer a public developer API.

sections.title: How much does the Seedance 2.5 API cost?
paragraphs: API pricing is per second of video and rises with resolution. When you pass a reference video, Kie bills a lower unit price on input plus output seconds, so a long reference clip can cost more than a text-only request.

rows: Kie, with video input (input plus output seconds)

callout.title: Workspace credits are a separate price
callout.text: These are provider API prices for developers. The browser workspace on this site charges product credits, listed on the pricing page.

sections.title: Seedance 2.5 API example with curl
paragraphs: Create a task with one POST request. The response returns a task ID immediately; the video is produced in the background.

examples.label: Create a task
examples.text:
curl -X POST https://api.kie.ai/api/v1/jobs/createTask \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $KIE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "bytedance/seedance-2-5",
    "callBackUrl": "https://your-domain.com/api/seedance/callback",
    "input": {
      "prompt": "A ceramic artist lifts a cobalt bowl into window light, slow dolly in.",
      "resolution": "720p",
      "duration": 5,
      "aspect_ratio": "16:9",
      "generate_audio": true
    }
  }'

callout.title: Do not generalize provider marketing
callout.text: Kie and fal currently list 1080p parameters for their 2.5 routes. This browser workspace exposes only 480p/720p. Distinguish requested size, returned file dimensions and verified native generation.

sections.title: The same request through fal
paragraphs: fal documents the model ID below and recommends its queue API for longer generations. In B2B use, send a stable, non-sensitive end_user_id as required by the provider—never an email or raw personal identifier.

steps.title: Create your own task first
steps.description: Reserve credits and persist your internal task ID before calling a provider.

steps.title: Store provider identity
steps.description: Save the actual provider, model ID and provider task ID so polling never guesses the route.

steps.title: Use idempotency boundaries
steps.description: Do not fall back to a second provider after a network timeout; the first request may already be running.

steps.title: Treat failure states explicitly
steps.description: Refund only on a confirmed terminal failure, not on a slow queue or temporary polling error.

steps.title: Copy durable outputs
steps.description: Provider result URLs may expire. Move completed videos to controlled storage according to user and provider terms.

steps.title: Observe cost and latency
steps.description: Log resolution, duration, provider, retries, final status and cost without recording sensitive prompts unnecessarily.

sections.title: API security and rights checks
bullets: Keep Kie and fal secrets in server-side environment variables; never prefix them as public client variables.
Validate URLs, MIME types, file sizes, counts, duration and allowlisted output settings before spending credits.
Rate-limit by account and internal end-user ID, not only by IP address.
Require users to have rights to every image, video, audio and character reference they submit.
Store the provider terms/version reviewed for your commercial-use decision.
Build moderation and appeal handling in addition to provider safety filters.

faqs.question: Is there a Seedance 2.5 API?
faqs.answer: Yes. Seedance 2.5 is available through third-party API providers including Kie and fal. ByteDance's own international API is not offered in every country, so many developers use a reseller.

faqs.question: How much does the Seedance 2.5 API cost per second?
faqs.answer: On October 3, 2026, Kie listed $0.14 per second at 480p, $0.315 at 720p and $0.79 at 1080p without video input. fal listed about $0.22 at 480p and $0.47 at 720p.

faqs.question: Is there an official public ByteDance Seedance 2.5 API?
faqs.answer: Official access and regional availability can differ from third-party access. This guide covers current Kie and fal provider routes; verify ByteDance or BytePlus documentation separately before describing a route as official.

faqs.question: Should I automatically fail over from Kie to fal?
faqs.answer: Only before a task may have been accepted, such as a validated provider rejection. Do not resubmit after a timeout or unknown server error because both providers might generate and charge.

faqs.question: Can I call these APIs from the browser?
faqs.answer: Do not expose provider secrets in client code. Send a validated request to your own server, create an internal task, then call the provider from the server.
